title: streaming: robust lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect/reconnect resume, and server timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Several customer incidents and internal canaries exposed edge cases in streaming lifecycle handling: client-side cancel signals were not always propagated to the server runtime, disconnects left orphaned KV cache or long-lived sessions, and reconnects could not resume partially-delivered streams in our OpenAI-compat proxy. This PR adds coordinated lifecycle controls to make streaming stable and predictable: 1) client cancel propagation (HTTP/WS) to cleanly abort server-side token generation and free runtime resources; 2) explicit disconnect handling that marks sessions as disconnected and starts a configurable resume-window timer; 3) reconnect/resume support that allows a client within the resume window to reattach to an existing session and continue receiving the rest of the stream (when supported by the model/runtime); 4) server-side idle/keepalive/timeouts to close orphaned sessions after a sensible default (30s) to avoid resource leaks and head-of-line blocking. Summary of changes: - runtime/streaming/lifecycle_manager.py: new SessionLifecycleManager that tracks session state transitions (active -> disconnected -> resumed -> closed), resume-window config, and coordinated cancellation semantics. - runtime/streaming/connection_handler.rs: lower-level changes to surface client disconnect/cancel events to the lifecycle manager and ensure KV cache cleanup on session close. - api/openai_compat/streaming_proxy.go: OpenAI compatibility layer updated to accept `Redwood-Session-Id` headers and attempt resume via `Resume-Session` handshake. Backwards-compatible: if no session id is provided or resume fails, the proxy falls back to starting a fresh stream. - sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py: new client helpers for session pinning, resume attempts, and cancel semantics. - tests/streaming/*: unit and integration tests covering cancel propagation, reconnect resume, and timeout behavior under load. - docs/streaming_lifecycle.md: new doc describing config knobs, SDK examples, and migration notes. Checklists: - [x] unit tests for lifecycle transitions - [x] integration test: client reconnect/resume - [x] load test to validate no regression in steady-state throughput - [x] docs and release notes - [x] feature-flag gating (enabled by default for new installs; opt-out via config) Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag `streaming_lifecycle_v1`; will ship on main but default-enabled for hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can opt-out via their config. We will monitor metrics (stream.session.resumed, stream.session.orphaned, runtime.kv.cache.size) and a set of regressions in the perf canary. Backward compatibility & migration: Existing clients that don't pass a session id will continue to work as before. Clients that wish to resume should persist `Redwood-Session-Id` returned in the initial response and pass it on reconnect attempts. Testing: Added deterministic unit tests and non-deterministic e2e tests guarded by a stable canary infra tag. Benchmarks show median streaming latency unchanged within noise; resource usage with aggressive resume windows was validated to avoid leaks. Known limitations: resuming is best-effort and depends on model/state characteristics; for some model variants we fallback to re-generation if resume is not possible. Monitoring & alerts: added new alert for orphaned-session rate exceeding threshold. Documentation: full examples and migration notes in docs/streaming_lifecycle.md.
commits: feat(streaming): add SessionLifecycleManager and session state tracking
fix(streaming): surface client cancel/disconnect events to runtime and ensure KV cleanup
feat(openai-compat): add Resume-Session handshake and Redwood-Session-Id header
chore(sdk): add helpers for session pinning and resume in Python SDK
test(streaming): add integration and load tests for reconnect/resume and timeouts
review_comments: Tomás Rivera (reviewer): Can we make the resume window configurable per-customer? Some enterprise customers want shorter windows. — Reply: yes, added `resume_window_ms` to the lifecycle config and wire it through Dedicated/Private configs.

Mei Chen (reviewer): Are we guaranteed to free KV cache on abort all code paths? I saw one path where a background task could hold a reference. — Reply: fixed by adding explicit drop and an ownership transfer on disconnect; added unit test that recreates the background-hold case.

Jordan Blake (reviewer): Please add metrics for session transitions and document SLO expectations for resumed vs restarted streams. — Reply: added stream.session.* metrics and documentation section with SLO notes.

Security review (automated): Ensure session ids are high entropy and not logged. — Reply: session ids use UUIDv4-like entropy and logging was audited; added filter for Redwood-Session-Id in log pipeline.
release_notes: Improved streaming lifecycle handling: client cancels now reliably abort server-side generation and free runtime resources.
Clients can reconnect within a configurable resume window to continue partially-delivered streams when supported by the model/runtime.
Server-side idle timeout added to close orphaned sessions and prevent resource leaks (default 30s).
OpenAI-compat: new headers `Redwood-Session-Id` and `Resume-Session` handshake; compatibility fallbacks included.
notes_for_ops: If orphaned sessions spike after rollout, consider lowering resume_window_ms and investigate client network churn.
